summary: Delaware County, NY lookout: a 45-foot windmill tower from 1910, replaced in 1919 by a 47-foot steel tower; lookout work ended in 1972 and the tower is closed on private land.

facts.design: 47-foot Aermotor LS40 steel lookout tower (1919), replacing a 45-foot modified windmill tower of 1910
facts.agency: Forest, Fish and Game Commission built the first tower in 1910; the Conservation Commission appointed observers from 1914

access.note: Stands on private land, closed to the public; sold to the landowner after the 1972 season per Wikipedia

events.note: May 1910 45-foot modified windmill tower, bought for $307.70 and erected by the Forest, Fish and Game Commission
Alfred Waterman of East Branch appointed observer for District No. 5 (Twadell Point)

Observer's cabin; Wikipedia says a cabin was on the mountain by 1916, while the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1917 report of seven new cabins, one at Twadell Point, and a 1924 report of a new cabin there
Windmill tower replaced by a 47-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower
Observer Alfred Waterman reported 12 fires so far that season, per a July 1924 Kingston Daily Freeman item quoted by Forest Lookouts
Fire observers agreed to scan the skies and report to the Albany Filter Center after a meeting with Air Force defense officials; Merton Williams of East Branch at Twadell Point
Fire lookout operations ended at the end of the 1972 season; the tower was then sold to the landowner

corrections.why: 13.7 m (45 ft) is the 1910 windmill tower. The tower standing since 1919 is 47 ft, about 14.3 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 45-foot figure belongs to the 1910 windmill; both NYSFFLA and Wikipedia give the 1919 steel tower as 47 feet.

notes_for_editor: Four sources agree on the 1910 windmill, the 1919 steel tower and the closed private status. Unresolved: the observer cabin date (Wikipedia by 1916 versus the 1917 annual report and a 1924 cabin report quoted by Forest Lookouts) and the summit elevation (NYSFFLA 2296 ft versus Wikipedia 2,293 ft); both are kept in the story and the elevation is not recorded in facts. The 'sold to the landowner' detail comes only from Wikipedia. The 1953 Air Force line is quoted by Forest Lookouts from The Oneonta Star and we did not open that original. Record changes: height_m proposed to 14.3 m; access unknown to private; staffing set to unstaffed from 1972; events added. No current photo or condition report found. About 2 page reads beyond the shared NY index, 1 WebSearch.
